D.t: Cyndi Munson trails by 5.8 and wins 21% of simulations. Closing it takes about 37,877 voters switching sides, or 75,754 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +14.9 and D +3.7. A normal polling error decides it.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Oklahoma, a projected net 65,059 votes; Tulsa, a projected net 31,062 votes; Cleveland, a projected net 14,153 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Cyndi Munson runs furthest behind in Le Flore, Washington, Mayes. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 43 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.12 points; Voters without a degree, 65% of voters, 46 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.25 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 65% of voters, 45 to 53, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.25 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Cyndi Munson: Immigration voters 20 to 78, Small counties 34 to 64, Incomes $125K and up 41 to 57. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
